title: Cooperative livelihoods become governable when public data, digital administration, and market access are rebuilt together in Lebanon
source_unit: ILO news report on the Lebanon cooperative-sector data and digital-modernization partnership, published 23 September 2026
geography: Lebanon, especially agricultural cooperatives and rural livelihoods involving Lebanese and Syrian workers and refugee-host communities

observations.period: September 2026 onward; national cooperative data and institutional-modernization partnership

denominator.unit: cooperatives registered with Lebanon's General Directorate of Cooperatives

data_gap.value: nationwide cooperative data had not been comprehensively updated since 2007

records_condition.value: records remain largely paper-based and fragmented

reform_route.value: requalification, nationwide data collection, stronger General Directorate capacity, and future digitalization of systems and services

observations.method: Official ILO account of a memorandum of understanding between the ILO, Lebanon's Ministry of Agriculture, and the General Directorate of Cooperatives; it is a partnership announcement, not an evaluation.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not establish how many registered cooperatives are active, how complete the legacy records are, or whether data modernization will improve service delivery, finance, job quality, or cooperative survival.
observations.subgroup: Agricultural cooperatives, farmers, workers, rural communities, Lebanese and Syrian workers, refugee-host communities, public administrators, and cooperative members.
observations.counterinterpretation: More data can improve targeting and transparency, but requalification or digital systems can also exclude informal, low-capacity, paper-poor, or politically unconnected cooperatives if access and support are uneven.

observations.period: 2026; cooperative livelihoods, displacement, and agricultural work

livelihood_role.value: cooperatives are described as supporting livelihoods and local economic development for refugees and host communities, particularly in rural areas

sector_risks.value: agriculture faces informality, low and irregular incomes, limited social protection, occupational safety and health risks, and child labour

governance_goal.value: better evidence and institutional capacity are intended to support cooperatives, decent jobs, livelihoods, and local development

observations.method: ILO programme framing connecting cooperative institutions to agricultural livelihoods, displacement contexts, and labour conditions.
observations.uncertainty: The account does not provide cooperative-level employment counts, refugee-host distribution, income data, safety incidence, child-labour prevalence, or evidence that cooperatives currently deliver equal benefits.
observations.subgroup: Refugee and host-community households, agricultural workers, women and youth where covered, cooperative members, informal workers, and local employers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cooperatives can support shared livelihoods but may reproduce local hierarchy, exclude nonmembers, or lack the capital and market power needed to improve wages and protection.

observations.period: 2024–2026; finance and job-support route for farmers and workers

denominator.unit: subsidized loans facilitated through broader ILO cooperation in Lebanon

market_access.unit: farmers and workers helped to access new buyers and international markets over the past two years

observations.method: ILO report of associated cooperation and reported outputs, including loans, jobs, and market access.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not identify loan recipients, repayment, additionality, job quality, job duration, market revenues, or whether access was cooperative-mediated or individually delivered.
observations.subgroup: Farmers, workers, cooperative members, small producers, rural businesses, buyers, exporters, and households dependent on agricultural income.
observations.counterinterpretation: Loan and buyer access can increase exposure to debt, market volatility, export standards, and unequal bargaining power; jobs created or sustained are not necessarily decent or durable.

observations.period: September 2026 onward; international partnership and cooperative-governance standards

denominator.unit: ILO–Lebanon–PROSPECTS partnership route for cooperative governance

partners.value: ILO, Lebanon's Ministry of Agriculture, General Directorate of Cooperatives, and PROSPECTS partnership

funding_context.value: the initiative is supported through PROSPECTS, funded by the Kingdom of the Netherlands

standard.value: the initiative aligns with ILO Recommendation No. 193 and cooperative-statistics guidelines

geopolitical_mechanism.value: external partnership and international standards are translated into domestic data, administrative, and rural-development capacity

observations.method: Official ILO account of a development partnership and its stated standards and institutional route.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not establish donor additionality, domestic ownership after partnership support, or whether international standards will be adapted effectively to local cooperative realities.
observations.subgroup: Lebanese public agencies, cooperative members, refugee and host communities, donors, international organizations, farmers, workers, and local development actors.
observations.counterinterpretation: International standards and donor-backed digitalization can improve comparability while also importing categories, reporting burdens, or priorities that do not fit local organizational practice.

related_sources.claim: ILO PROSPECTS partnership context in Lebanon.
ILO Recommendation No. 193 on the promotion of cooperatives.

boundary: This record adds a cooperative-institution route linking data visibility, digital public administration, rural livelihoods, refugee-host economies, finance, market access, decent work, and international development standards. It is an official partnership announcement with reported associated outputs, not evidence of cooperative survival, representative job quality, causal finance effects, or implemented digital-service outcomes.
